entries.meaning: Work has 3 distinct senses.
examples: I work for a small firm downtown.
She worked late three nights in a row.
He has been working here since 2019.
The elevator doesn't work again.
The medicine worked within an hour.
Their plan has worked better than anyone expected.
Can you work the projector?
She worked the register while the manager was out.
He has been working that crane for twenty years.

senses.head: To do a job, especially one you are paid for
examples: I work for a small firm downtown.
She worked late three nights in a row.
He has been working here since 2019.

senses.head: For a machine, a system, or a plan to do what it is supposed to do
examples: The elevator doesn't work again.
The medicine worked within an hour.
Their plan has worked better than anyone expected.

senses.head: To operate a machine or a piece of equipment
examples: Can you work the projector?
She worked the register while the manager was out.

entries.transitivity: both — transitive (work long hours), intransitive (she works downtown)
entries.contrast: Work FOR a company, work AT a place, work ON a project, work WITH people. The preposition changes the meaning, not the verb.
entries.phrasal verbs: work around · work in · work off · work on, work for, work with · work out · work out · work out · work out · work out to · work through · work up · work up · work up to

senses.head: To create something over time, or to grow and become more advanced
examples: Our team develops software for hospitals.
They developed the prototype in four months.
We are developing a cheaper version.

senses.head: To treat photographic film with chemicals so that the pictures appear
examples: A few shops still develop film.
He developed the roll in a darkroom.
The photos are being developed now.

senses.head: To begin to have an illness, a fault, or a feeling
examples: Some patients develop a rash from this drug.
She developed a fever overnight.
The engine has developed a strange rattle.

entries.русский: разрабатывать, разработать; развивать, развиваться; проявлять, проявить (плёнку, снимки); заболевать, заболеть; появляться (о симптоме, о неисправности)
entries.transitivity: both — transitive (develop a product), intransitive (the market developed quickly)
entries.contrast: No doubled p and no final e: developed, developing, development.

entries.meaning: To plan how something will look or work before it is made. ---
examples: She designs packaging for food brands.
They designed the store layout themselves.
The system was designed for small teams.
entries.contrast: The g is silent: di-ZYN. It comes back in designate and designation.

entries.meaning: Produce has 3 distinct senses.
examples: The plant produces four thousand units a day.
They produced the entire run in Mexico.
Most of our parts are produced locally.
He produced a driver's license from his back pocket.
You have to be able to produce proof of insurance.
Having produced no receipt, she was refused a refund.
She produces a late-night talk show.
He produced three albums for the band.
The film was produced on a shoestring budget.

senses.head: To make or grow something, especially in large amounts
examples: The plant produces four thousand units a day.
They produced the entire run in Mexico.
Most of our parts are produced locally.

senses.head: To bring something out and show it
examples: He produced a driver's license from his back pocket.
You have to be able to produce proof of insurance.
Having produced no receipt, she was refused a refund.

senses.head: To be in charge of the money and the organization behind a film, a show, or a record
examples: She produces a late-night talk show.
He produced three albums for the band.
The film was produced on a shoestring budget.

entries.русский: производить, произвести; выпускать, изготавливать; предъявлять, предъявить; доставать, достать (и показать); продюсировать, быть продюсером (фильма, альбома)
entries.contrast: The verb is pruh-DOOSS; the noun produce, meaning fruit and vegetables, is PROH-dooss.

entries.meaning: Manufacture has 2 distinct senses.
examples: They manufacture medical equipment in Ohio.
These chips were manufactured in Taiwan.
The company has been manufacturing here since 1962.
Don't manufacture an excuse — just tell them the truth.
The article claims that agents manufactured the evidence.
The whole scandal was manufactured by a rival campaign.

senses.head: To make goods in a factory, usually in large quantities
examples: They manufacture medical equipment in Ohio.
These chips were manufactured in Taiwan.
The company has been manufacturing here since 1962.

senses.head: To invent something false, such as an excuse or evidence
examples: Don't manufacture an excuse — just tell them the truth.
The article claims that agents manufactured the evidence.
The whole scandal was manufactured by a rival campaign.

entries.русский: производить, изготавливать, изготовить; фабриковать, сфабриковать; выдумывать, выдумать

entries.meaning: To advertise and sell a product to a particular group of buyers. ---
examples: They market the service to small businesses.
The drink was marketed as a health product.
We are marketing it mainly through social media.
entries.contrast: Stress is on the first syllable, so the t does not double: marketed, marketing.

entries.meaning: To tell the public about a product, a service, or a job. ---
examples: We advertise openings on three job boards.
They advertised the sale for two weeks.
The job was never advertised publicly.
entries.transitivity: both — transitive (advertise the position), intransitive (we advertise on the radio)
entries.contrast: Always -ise, in America too: advertise, never advertize. Compare organize and analyze, which do change.

entries.meaning: To provide someone with something they need, especially goods. ---
examples: Two farms supply all of our produce.
They supplied the parts at cost.
The materials are supplied by a local firm.
entries.contrast: Consonant plus -y: supplies, supplied, but supplying keeps the y. Supply someone WITH something.

entries.meaning: To buy something, especially in formal or business language. ---
examples: The city purchases its vehicles through a state contract.
They purchased the building in 2019.
Equipment purchased this year is still under warranty.

entries.meaning: Bill has 2 distinct senses.
examples: We bill clients at the end of the month.
They billed us twice for the same visit.
You will be billed only after delivery.
The company bills itself as the cheapest carrier in the state.
The fight was billed as the match of the century.
They're billing the new place as a family restaurant.

senses.head: To send someone a statement of how much they owe
examples: We bill clients at the end of the month.
They billed us twice for the same visit.
You will be billed only after delivery.

senses.head: To advertise or describe something publicly as being a particular thing
examples: The company bills itself as the cheapest carrier in the state.
The fight was billed as the match of the century.
They're billing the new place as a family restaurant.

entries.русский: выставлять счёт, выставить счёт; объявлять, рекламировать (как); подавать (как)
entries.contrast: Bill someone FOR something: they billed us for the repair.

entries.meaning: To provide the money for a project or an organization. ---
examples: Two investors fund most of the research.
The state funded half the construction.
The program is funded through 2027.

entries.meaning: To plan how much money you will spend on something. ---
examples: We budget about five percent for training.
They budgeted twenty thousand dollars for the move.
Nobody had budgeted for a second audit.
entries.русский: планировать бюджет, закладывать в бюджет; выделять средства
entries.transitivity: both — transitive (budget ten thousand dollars), intransitive (budget for repairs)
entries.contrast: Stress is on the first syllable, so the t stays single: budgeted, budgeting. Budget FOR something.

entries.meaning: To become larger, or to make something larger. ---
examples: Small firms expand slowly at first.
They expanded into Canada last year.
We have been expanding the team all spring.
entries.transitivity: both — transitive (expand the range), intransitive (the firm expanded)

entries.meaning: To buy or obtain something, especially a company, a property, or a skill. ---
examples: Big platforms acquire small startups every month.
They acquired the rights for two million dollars.
The company was acquired by a German group.

entries.meaning: Establish has 2 distinct senses.
examples: New owners usually establish their own rules.
They established the firm in a garage.
The company was established in 1948.
The autopsy established the cause of death.
We need to establish who was in the building that night.
It has been established that the fire started in the kitchen.

senses.head: To start an organization or a system that is meant to last
examples: New owners usually establish their own rules.
They established the firm in a garage.
The company was established in 1948.

senses.head: To find out a fact and prove it beyond doubt
examples: The autopsy established the cause of death.
We need to establish who was in the building that night.
It has been established that the fire started in the kitchen.

entries.русский: основывать, основать; устанавливать, налаживать; устанавливать, установить (факт); выяснять, выяснить
entries.contrast: After -sh the third person adds -es: establishes.

entries.meaning: To start a company, a school, or an organization. ---
examples: It takes nerve to found a company alone.
She founded the agency at twenty-six.
The firm was founded by two former teachers.
entries.contrast: This is a regular verb: found - founded - founded. Do not confuse it with found, the past of find. He founded the company; he found the keys.

entries.meaning: Own has 2 distinct senses.
examples: She owns two restaurants downtown.
They owned the building before the bank took it.
The chain is owned by a family in Texas.
A good manager owns her mistakes.
He owned the error and apologized to the team.
She has owned her part in the failure.

senses.head: To have something as your property
examples: She owns two restaurants downtown.
They owned the building before the bank took it.
The chain is owned by a family in Texas.

senses.head: To admit a mistake and accept responsibility for it
examples: A good manager owns her mistakes.
He owned the error and apologized to the team.
She has owned her part in the failure.

entries.русский: владеть, иметь в собственности; признавать (вину, ошибку), брать ответственность на себя
entries.contrast: Own describes a state, so it is rarely used in the -ing form: she owns it, not she is owning it.

entries.meaning: To pay to use a property for a period, or to let someone use yours for payment. ---
examples: We rent the second floor.
They rented a warehouse near the airport.
The office has been rented to a law firm.
entries.transitivity: both — transitive (rent an office), intransitive (we rent, we do not own)
entries.contrast: Rent FROM the owner, rent TO a tenant. American English uses rent for both sides; the British often say let for the owner's side.

entries.meaning: To make something better, or to become better. ---
examples: Small changes improve the process a lot.
Delivery times improved after the new software.
Service has been improving since January.
entries.transitivity: both — transitive (improve the process), intransitive (results improved)

entries.meaning: To become greater in number or amount, or to make something greater. ---
examples: We increase prices once a year.
Sales increased by nine percent.
Rent has increased every year since 2020.
entries.transitivity: both — transitive (increase the price), intransitive (costs increased)
entries.contrast: The verb is stressed at the end, in-KREESS; the noun at the front, IN-kreess, as in a pay increase.

entries.meaning: Reduce has 3 distinct senses.
examples: We need to reduce overtime.
They reduced the headcount by twenty.
Costs have been reduced by a third.
Reduce the sauce until it coats the back of a spoon.
She reduced the stock by half.
The wine was reducing on the back burner.
Don't let him reduce you to tears.
The fire reduced the barn to a pile of ash.
Whole blocks had been reduced to rubble.

senses.head: To make something smaller in size, amount, or price
examples: We need to reduce overtime.
They reduced the headcount by twenty.
Costs have been reduced by a third.

senses.head: To boil a liquid so that some of the water evaporates and the flavor gets stronger
examples: Reduce the sauce until it coats the back of a spoon.
She reduced the stock by half.
The wine was reducing on the back burner.

senses.head: To bring someone or something down to a much worse state
examples: Don't let him reduce you to tears.
The fire reduced the barn to a pile of ash.
Whole blocks had been reduced to rubble.

entries.русский: сокращать, сократить; снижать, уменьшать; уваривать, уварить; выпаривать; доводить (до слёз); превращать, обращать (в руины)
entries.contrast: American ri-DOOSS, not ri-DYOOSS.

entries.meaning: To finish something, or to fill in every part of a form. ---
examples: Please complete the form before Friday.
They completed the building two months early.
The training must be completed within thirty days.

entries.meaning: To bring something to an end, or to come to an end. ---
examples: He usually finishes by six.
She finished the report on the train.
We are finishing the last section today.
entries.transitivity: both — transitive (finish the report), intransitive (the meeting finished at five)
entries.contrast: Finish DOING something, never finish to do: I finished writing the report.
entries.phrasal verbs: finish off · finish off · finish up

entries.meaning: To succeed in reaching a goal after effort. ---
examples: Few teams achieve that in a single quarter.
They achieved record sales in December.
Nothing would have been achieved without her.
entries.contrast: Spelled -ie-: achieve, achieved, not acheive.

entries.meaning: To finish something successfully, especially something difficult. ---
examples: Long meetings rarely accomplish much.
The team accomplished a great deal in six weeks.
We have accomplished everything on the list.
entries.contrast: After -sh the third person adds -es: accomplishes.

entries.meaning: Fail has 3 distinct senses.
examples: Most new restaurants fail in the first year.
The supplier failed to deliver on time.
Two of the three pilot projects have failed.
The brakes failed halfway down the hill.
If the power fails, the generator starts automatically.
Doctors told him his kidneys were failing.
The professor failed half the class.
They'll fail you if you skip the final.
She was failed for copying someone else's answers.

senses.head: To not succeed, or to not do something that you should have done
body: (терпеть неудачу, провалиться; не суметь, не справиться)
examples: Most new restaurants fail in the first year.
The supplier failed to deliver on time.
Two of the three pilot projects have failed.

senses.head: To stop working the way it should
body: (отказывать, отказать; выходить из строя, переставать работать)
examples: The brakes failed halfway down the hill.
If the power fails, the generator starts automatically.
Doctors told him his kidneys were failing.

senses.head: To judge a student's work as not good enough to pass
examples: The professor failed half the class.
They'll fail you if you skip the final.
She was failed for copying someone else's answers.

entries.русский: терпеть неудачу, провалиться; не суметь, не справиться; отказывать, отказать; выходить из строя, переставать работать; ставить неудовлетворительную оценку; заваливать, завалить (студента)
entries.transitivity: both — transitive (fail the exam), intransitive (the business failed)
entries.contrast: Fail TO DO something: he failed to answer, not he failed answering.

entries.meaning: Serve has 4 distinct senses.
examples: One office serves the whole region.
He served as treasurer for six years.
Over a thousand clients are served each month.
An old door serves as our kitchen table.
The gym served as a shelter during the storm.
That hallway has served as a gallery for years.
He will serve eighteen months.
She served two tours overseas.
He has served most of his sentence already.
She serves harder than anyone else on the tour.
He served four aces in one game.
He was serving for the match when the rain started.

senses.head: To work for a person, an organization, or a group of customers
examples: One office serves the whole region.
He served as treasurer for six years.
Over a thousand clients are served each month.

senses.head: To be used as something, or to be useful for a purpose
examples: An old door serves as our kitchen table.
The gym served as a shelter during the storm.
That hallway has served as a gallery for years.

senses.head: To spend a period of time in prison or in the armed forces
examples: He will serve eighteen months.
She served two tours overseas.
He has served most of his sentence already.

senses.head: In tennis or volleyball, to put the ball into play by hitting it
examples: She serves harder than anyone else on the tour.
He served four aces in one game.
He was serving for the match when the rain started.

entries.русский: обслуживать, обслужить; служить, работать (на должности); служить (в качестве), использоваться как; отбывать, отбыть (срок); служить (в армии); подавать, подать (мяч)
entries.transitivity: both — transitive (serve customers), intransitive (she served on the board)

entries.meaning: Process has 2 distinct senses.
examples: The bank processes refunds in five days.
They processed my application the same week.
Your order is being processed.
I need a few days to process what happened.
She is still processing the news.
We never really processed the loss as a family.

senses.head: To deal with documents, data, or materials in an official or standard way
examples: The bank processes refunds in five days.
They processed my application the same week.
Your order is being processed.

senses.head: To take the time to accept and come to terms with a difficult experience or feeling
examples: I need a few days to process what happened.
She is still processing the news.
We never really processed the loss as a family.

entries.русский: обрабатывать, обработать; оформлять, рассматривать; осмысливать, осмыслить; переваривать (пережитое), справляться с эмоциями
entries.contrast: American English stresses the first syllable and uses the LOT vowel: PRAH-sess.

entries.meaning: File has 3 distinct senses.
examples: Most companies file their taxes in March.
She filed a complaint with the labor board.
The paperwork was filed a week late.
She stopped to file a broken nail.
He filed the edge of the key until it fit the lock.
The weld has been filed smooth.
The students filed into the auditorium.
We watched the jurors file silently to their seats.
Mourners were filing past the casket all afternoon.

senses.head: To send an official document to an authority, or to store papers in order
examples: Most companies file their taxes in March.
She filed a complaint with the labor board.
The paperwork was filed a week late.

senses.head: To smooth or shape something by rubbing it with a rough metal tool
examples: She stopped to file a broken nail.
He filed the edge of the key until it fit the lock.
The weld has been filed smooth.

senses.head: To walk somewhere in a line, one person behind another
examples: The students filed into the auditorium.
We watched the jurors file silently to their seats.
Mourners were filing past the casket all afternoon.

entries.русский: подавать (документы), подать; регистрировать, подшивать; подпиливать, подпилить (ногти); опиливать, зачищать; идти вереницей, проходить гуськом; выстраиваться цепочкой
entries.transitivity: both — transitive (file a complaint), intransitive (file for bankruptcy)
entries.contrast: Drop the -e before -ing: filing. File FOR bankruptcy, file a complaint WITH an office.

entries.meaning: To pay an outside company to do work that your own staff used to do. ---
examples: Many firms outsource payroll.
They outsourced customer support to a call center.
Half of our technical work is now outsourced.

entries.meaning: To make a process run by machines or software instead of by people. ---
examples: We automate anything we do more than twice.
They automated the whole billing cycle.
Most of the reporting is now automated.

entries.meaning: Distribute has 2 distinct senses.
examples: Two warehouses distribute to the whole West Coast.
They distributed the agenda before the meeting.
Bonuses are distributed in December.
Distribute the weight evenly across both axles.
The paint was not distributed evenly, so the wall looks streaky.
One vent distributes warm air to the whole upstairs.

senses.head: To give things out to a number of people, or to supply goods to stores
examples: Two warehouses distribute to the whole West Coast.
They distributed the agenda before the meeting.
Bonuses are distributed in December.

senses.head: To spread something evenly over an area or a surface
examples: Distribute the weight evenly across both axles.
The paint was not distributed evenly, so the wall looks streaky.
One vent distributes warm air to the whole upstairs.

entries.русский: распределять, распределить; распространять, раздавать; распределять, распределить (равномерно)
